profile.headline: Software Engineer, Applied Mathematician, Physicist
profile.summary: Software engineer with a specialization in scientific computing and expertise in mathematical modeling, physics, and machine learning. Passionate about finding creative solutions to complex problems.

positions.title: Instructor
positions.locationName: Palo Alto, California, United States · Remote
positions.description: Provide mentorship to students on tailored projects that implement fundamental machine learning algorithms and intricate deep learning models for diverse applications using frameworks such as Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow.
positions.insights: Skills: Keras · Matplotlib · Deep Neural Networks (DNN) · Deep Learning · NumPy · Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) · SciPy · Large Language Models (LLM) · Pandas (Software) · PyTorch

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Promoted within 6 months to the MATLAB Data Science Types team, whose mission is to develop tools that aid workflows involving richly-structured data. Enhancing a datatype conversion method for time stamped workflows and introducing a new property in existing abstract datatypes to facilitate metadata retrieval and type conversions are examples of some development projects.

positions.title: Engineer
positions.description: Member of the MATLAB Math team. Collaborated with scientists, engineers, and academics to understand their software needs for optimal productivity. Contributed to the internal knowledge base by publishing technical articles on effective solutions to issues raised by MATLAB users.

positions.title: Doctoral Researcher
positions.description: Member of the Experimental Soft Condensed Matter Group led by Prof. David A. Weitz. Demonstrated proficiency in vertical integration by designing, fabricating, and executing a novel experiment to study colloidal suspension dynamics. Optimized the lab's gas supply management system, eliminating situations that previously led to gas supply outages. Served as a lab safety officer for over two years.

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Fellow
positions.description: Provided mentorship and academic support to hundreds of students in the areas of mathematical modeling, software engineering, and high performance computing. Courses taught: Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations (AM 105: Spring 2018), Nonlinear Dynamical Systems (AM 108: Spring 2019, Fall 2020), Systems Development for Computational Science (CS 107: Fall 2021), and High Performance Computing for Science and Engineering (CS 205: Spring 2022).

positions.title: Graduate Student Researcher
positions.description: Member of the Westervelt Group led by Prof. Robert M. Westervelt. Designed a mechanism to optimize the lab's process for fabricating semiconductor devices to study electron transport in two-dimensional materials.
positions.insights: Skills: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) · Nanofabrication · Electron Beam Lithography · AutoCAD · Mechanical Engineering

positions.title: Undergraduate Student Researcher
positions.description: Simulated dynamic binary star systems using an open-source computational astrophysics library to study the effects of metallicity on the orbital period. Worked under the supervision of Dr. Lennart van Haaften and Prof. Tom Maccarone.

projects.title: Parameter Estimation in Dynamical Systems
projects.description:
C++ library designed to perform gradient descent optimization on systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for parameter estimation. Seamlessly interfaces with BLAS/LAPACK, harnessing optimized numerical linear algebra routines to enhance computational performance and features an implementation of the Dormand-Prince 5(4) method, enabling efficient and accurate numerical solutions of ODEs.

GitHub repo: https://github.com/erruiz/param_est_odes

projects.title: Computational Photography
projects.description: C++ library designed for fundamental computation photography operations as part of a course project for MIT 6.865: Advanced Computational Photography.
